documents.title: Dissertation & Thesis Handbook (Generative AI section)
documents.summary: A short Generative AI section in the Graduate School thesis and dissertation handbook. It allows AI to support thinking, research and writing only after consulting the committee chair, bans AI-generated writing in the thesis, and requires detailed citation of AI used in research. Violations count as academic dishonesty.
documents.stance_why: AI "can be used as a tool for supporting thinking, research, and writing" but only after consulting the chair, and "graduate students cannot use AI-generated writing in their thesis or dissertation"; permitted only for narrow uses with a firm ban on generated text, so restrict.

units.why: The handbook opens its AI section by saying AI "blurs ethical boundaries, outstripping traditional policies"; this is a framing principle for the section, so it is informs/general. P56 (framework preamble) fits better than P54 because it states purpose, not a review commitment.
units.anchor: AI is a rapidly shifting new tool that blurs ethical boundaries
units.frag_end: traditional policies and rules regarding plagiarism

units.why: "AI can be used as a tool for supporting thinking, research, and writing" allows AI for thesis work, a permission with the condition in the next sentences, so modality may and unit_stance permit. P02 (permit by default) fits; the conditions are coded separately.
units.anchor: AI can be used as a tool for supporting thinking, research, and writing

units.why: "AI cannot be used to replace these acts" (thinking, research, writing) keeps the student as the primary thinker, so P32 rather than P19 which is about submitted generated text, coded separately.
units.anchor: AI cannot be used to replace these acts

units.why: "they must consult with their committee chair beforehand" requires students to ask before using generative AI in research; P10 (ask first) fits better than P04 because it is about the student's duty to ask.
units.anchor: they must consult with their committee chair beforehand

units.why: "They must adhere to guidance from their chair" makes the committee chair the decider of what AI use is allowed, i.e. per-supervisor rule setting, so P04.
units.anchor: They must adhere to guidance from their chair.

units.why: "graduate students cannot use AI-generated writing in their thesis or dissertation" bans submitting AI-produced text as the thesis, so must-not, prohibit, P19.
units.anchor: graduate students cannot use AI-generated writing in their thesis or dissertation

units.why: "that use must be detailed and cited according to the academic publishing guidelines in their field" requires disclosure of AI used in the research process, so P24 (disclose with submission).
units.anchor: that use must be detailed and cited according to the academic publishing guidelines

units.why: "students must be able to clearly explain and replicate the process of using AI" requires understanding and defending the AI-assisted research process when asked, so P30 rather than P34 since no review format is specified.
units.anchor: students must be able to clearly explain and replicate the process of using AI

units.why: "Failure to adhere to this policy constitutes academic dishonesty" classes violations as misconduct, so P36.
units.anchor: Failure to adhere to this policy constitutes academic dishonesty

notes: Only the Graduate School thesis handbook AI section was included; scope is graduate theses and dissertations. Paragraph on plagiarism/attribution under Academic Dishonesty not coded as it does not mention AI.
